key_insight: A conditional neural field, strengthened with Fourier features, relative error loss, ensembling, and cross-validation, can accurately predict aerodynamic wall distributions on complex aircraft geometry with very limited CFD training data.
engineering_relevance: This offers a compact surrogate model for rapid aerodynamic surface prediction on realistic configurations like the NASA Common Research Model, reducing reliance on expensive high-fidelity CFD runs.
method: Input spatial coordinates, surface normals, and operating conditions to a coordinate-based neural field.
Use Fourier feature encoding plus a relative squared error objective aligned with the competition metric.
Improve robustness with ensemble learning and k-fold cross-validation under limited data.
evidence_signal: On the hidden test set, the method scored 8.81, beating the organizer baseline score of 8.64 while using about three orders of magnitude fewer trainable parameters.
watch_item: Performance depends on carefully tuned feature encoding, loss design, and ensemble strategy, so generalization to new geometries or broader flow regimes may require additional validation.
paper_title: Neural Field Ensembles for Aerodynamic Surface Prediction: Winning Solution to the ONERA CRM Wall Distribution 2025 Challenge
